concepts.def: A novel product, process or idea that did not exist before, often protected by a patent to stop others copying it.
The successful commercial development and adoption of an invention, turning a new idea into a product that the market accepts.
Product development driven by an identified consumer need or demand, where signals from the market determine what should be designed.
Product development driven by new technology or materials, where research breakthroughs create products before clear consumer demand exists.
Dividing a market into distinct groups of consumers who share characteristics such as age, income or lifestyle, so products can be targeted.
The identity of a company or product, including its name, values and visual style, which shapes consumer perception and loyalty.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Innovation & Markets — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Innovation & Markets brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Innovation & Markets.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Innovation differs from invention because innovation is:
options: The successful commercial development and adoption of an idea in the market
Any sketch of a new product
The legal document protecting an idea
Always a completely new scientific discovery

mcqs.q: A product developed in response to an identified consumer demand is an example of:
options: Technology push
Market pull
Strategic drift
Continuous production

mcqs.q: Which scenario best illustrates technology push?
options: A survey reveals customers want quieter vacuum cleaners
A retailer requests a cheaper version of an existing toy
Customers complain about battery life so capacity is increased
A new material from a research lab inspires an entirely new product category
Selling one identical product to everyone
Splitting the company into departments
Dividing consumers into groups with shared characteristics to target products at them
Removing a product from the market

mcqs.q: What is the difference between invention and innovation?
options: They are the same thing - every invention is automatically an innovation.
Innovation only refers to changes in company logos.
A brand is the barcode printed on the packaging.
Invention is creating a genuinely new idea or device; innovation is successfully developing and commercialising it so the market adopts it.

mcqs.q: Does market pull mean a company pushes its products onto the market?
options: Innovation only refers to changes in company logos.
Yes - market pull is when firms push advertising at consumers.
No - market pull means consumer demand pulls new products into existence; technology push is when new technology drives development before demand exists.
Market pull means withdrawing products that fail.

mcqs.q: Is a brand just a logo?
options: No - a brand is the whole identity and perception of a product or company, including its values, reputation and customer experience; the logo is only one visible symbol.
Yes - the brand and the logo are the same thing.
A brand is the barcode printed on the packaging.
Market pull means withdrawing products that fail.

sequence.def: First to buy: risk-takers who try unproven products
Opinion leaders whose approval drives the market
Deliberate buyers join once benefits are proven
Sceptics buy only when most people already have
